title: Metabarcoding Based Gut Content Analysis of Arachnids
author: Yuval Zaltz
materials: DNA extraction follows the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit protocol. Add 180 µL Buffer ATL to the isolated tissue in the 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes. As per the Qiagen protocol, sub-sample tissue exceeding approximately 25 mg .

The samples should now be checked for successful amplification, contamination in negatives and any secondary banding. Gel electrophoresis will achieve this, but digital systems like the Qiagen Qiaxcel will do this and facilitate equalisation by generating amplicon-specific DNA concentrations. Gel electrophoresis is nevertheless described below.

DNA extraction follows the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit protocol. Add 180 µL Buffer ATL to the isolated tissue in the 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes. As per the Qiagen protocol, sub-sample tissue exceeding approximately 25 mg .

steps.title: Collect and Store Arachnids
steps.instruction: Collect arachnids from study sites, place them into 100% volume ethanol, and store at -20 °C until DNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract Gut Contents
steps.instruction: Isolate the abdomen and extract DNA using a spin-column method. The process differs slightly by taxon.

substeps.instruction: For scorpions: Use bleach-sterilised tools to cut the abdomen open and scrape innards into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
For spiders: Use bleach-sterilised tools to remove the abdomen and place it into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Homogenise abdomens with a tissue homogeniser for approximately 3 seconds or until fully homogenised (sterilise homogeniser head with bleach, water, and ethanol between samples).
Add 20 µL Proteinase K to tubes.
Incubate on a thermoshaker at 150 rpm, 56 °C for 2 hours.
Add 200 µL Buffer AL and vortex/shake to mix.
Add 200 µL 100% (v/v) ethanol and vortex/shake to mix.
Pipette the mixture (~600 µL) into a spin column in a 2 mL collection tube; centrifuge at 6000 x g for 1 minute and discard flow-through.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW1 to the column; centrifuge at 6000 x g for 1 minute and discard flow-through.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW2 to the column; centrifuge at 20000 x g for 3 minutes and discard flow-through.

Place column in a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 200 µL Buffer AE, incubate at room temperature for 1 minute, and centrifuge at 6000 x g for 1 minute (repeat elution if higher mass yield is needed).

steps.title: Plan PCR Plate Layout
steps.instruction: Design the distribution of samples and controls on the PCR plates.

substeps.instruction: Include negative controls in each row and column (including DNA extraction negative controls).
Include positive controls (mixed species not in the study system) adjacent to negative controls and samples on separate rows/columns.
Include blank controls (no reagents or no primers) adjacent to negative controls and samples on separate rows/columns.
Prepare separate plates for different PCR primer pairs based on their annealing temperatures.
Plan for replicates (e.g., triplicates) for optimal accuracy.

steps.title: Prepare PCR Mastermix and Plate
steps.instruction: Assemble the PCR reactions using a mastermix and specific primers.

substeps.instruction: Prepare mastermix for 25 µL reactions: 422.4 µL molecular grade water (DNase free) and 528 µL 2X hot-start PCR mastermix for a full plate (adjust for overage).
Option A (96-well pipette): Create a primer plate with both primers at 2.5 µM. Add 20 µL mastermix to PCR plate, then 2 µL of primer mix per well.

Option B (Manual): Make eight mastermixes (for 12 samples each) containing 264 µL mastermix and 26.4 µL of 2.5 µM forward primer. Distribute 22 µL of this mix per well across rows, then add 2 µL of reverse primer per well in columns.
Add 1 µL DNA to sample and positive control wells; add 1 µL molecular grade water to negative controls (except extraction negatives).
Distribute one drop (~20 µL) of mineral oil into each well to prevent evaporation.
Briefly centrifuge the plate to ensure oil is above the mix and no bubbles exist.

steps.title: Run Primary PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify the target DNA using a thermocycler.

substeps.instruction: Load the plate into the thermocycler.
Set the temperature regime to match the enzyme (including hot-start activation) and the annealing temperature of the primers.
Optional: Run a temperature gradient PCR with known samples to optimize temperatures.

steps.title: Verify PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Use agarose gel electrophoresis to confirm successful amplification and lack of contamination.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a gel tank with 1X TBE buffer.
Prepare a 2% (w/v) agarose gel: weigh 3 g agarose into 150 mL 1X TBE buffer, heat in microwave until bubbling, swirl to remove lumps, cool for 30 seconds, and add 3 µL gel dye (e.g., SYBRSafe).
Pour mixture into a mould with comb tips and let set for 25 minutes.
Prepare samples: add 2 µL of PCR product and 2 µL of 1X DNA dye to a new plate.
Load 4 µL DNA gel ladder on each side of each row, then load 4 µL of dyed PCR product into other wells.
Run the gel at 120 V and 120 A for 25 minutes.
Visualize under UV or blue light in a contained dock.

steps.title: Merge PCR Replicates
steps.instruction: If triplicates were run, merge them into a single plate per primer pair.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 20 µL from each well of two plates into the corresponding well of the third plate (assuming 25 µL initial volume).
Briefly centrifuge the merged plate to move oil to the top.
Tip: Insert pipette tip fully to the bottom and release sharply to avoid taking up viscous oil.

steps.title: Prepare SPRI Bead Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare 1X and 0.1X SPRI bead solutions for purification.

substeps.instruction: If using Sera-Mag Magnetic SpeedBeads (carboxylated, 1 µm, 3 EDAC/PA5): Wash 1 mL beads twice with TE+Tween buffer (10 mM Tris base, 1 mM EDTA, 0.05% Tween 20, pH 8.0) using a magnet.
To the washed beads, add: 25 mL 5 M NaCl, 3.582 mL molecular grade water, 0.168 mL 1 N HCl, 0.5 mL 1 M Tris base, and 0.5 mL 0.1 M disodium EDTA.
Add 20 mL of 50% PEG to create a 1X bead solution.

To create a 0.1X solution: Add 5 mL of 1X bead solution to 45 mL of a mix containing 25 mL 5 M NaCl, 3.582 mL molecular grade water, 0.168 mL 1 N HCl, 0.5 mL 1 M Tris base, 0.5 mL 0.1 M disodium EDTA, and 20 mL 50% PEG.

steps.title: Purify PCR Products with Beads
steps.instruction: Use 0.1X SPRI beads to clean the PCR products.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 20 µL of 0.1X SPRI bead solution into each well of a new 96-well plate (or a volume equivalent to the available PCR product).
Add 20 µL of PCR product (avoiding oil) to the beads; vortex at 1500 rpm for 1 minute.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes, then place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Remove all but 5 µL of the mixture from each well.
Wash twice: add 200 µL 80% ethanol, remove, then add another 200 µL 80% ethanol and remove as completely as possible.
Add 10 µL molecular grade water, shake at 1500 rpm for 1 minute, and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Pool and Final Purify DNA
steps.instruction: Pool the purified samples and perform a final size-selection purification.

substeps.instruction: Pool 8 µL from each well into a single tube (leaving beads behind).
Mix by flicking/inverting and transfer 700 µL to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Add 700 µL 1X magnetic beads (or 560 µL for a 0.8X ratio if amplicons are ~350 bp) and vortex.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes, then place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Wash twice with 400 µL 80% ethanol.
Remove ethanol completely, centrifuge briefly, and air-dry until beads transition from 'glossy' to 'matte'.
Add 100 µL molecular grade water, vortex, and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes and remove 95 µL of the water into a new tube as the library.

steps.title: Prepare Sequencing Libraries
steps.instruction: Add sequencing adapters via a second PCR.

substeps.instruction: Quantify library concentration (e.g., Qubit dsDNA assay).
Dilute library to ≤ 5000 µg/µL (≤5 ng/µL) in molecular grade water.
Assemble reaction per library in a tube with a drop of mineral oil: 7.5 µL 2X hot-start PCR mastermix, 14 µL molecular grade water, 1.5 µL Nextera sequencing adapter primer mix, and 5 µL DNA library.
Briefly centrifuge and run in a thermocycler for 12 cycles using appropriate enzyme/primer settings.

steps.title: Final QC and Pooling
steps.instruction: Verify adapter addition and pool libraries for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Quantify final library concentration (e.g., Qubit).
Assess amplicon size (e.g., TapeStation or gel) to confirm adapters were added (amplicons should be longer than before the second PCR).
Pool libraries equimolarly based on fmol (rather than ng/µL) to account for different molecular weights of different primer pairs.
Consult sequencing provider for required fmol and volume (µL) based on their specific sequencer and cartridge.
